Percentile rank of the subject's Y within peers (0-1). Whether a

composite uses the standardized, direction-adjusted form.

(raw, before the direction convention is applied).

direction.description: Rich/cheap sign convention of the Y metric.

excluded_reason.description: Why the composite leaves this dimension out; `None` when it is used.

peer_stats.description:
Statistics of Y over every peer that has it, including peers missing X;
`None` when no peer has it.

percentile.description: Share of those peer Y values at or below the subject's, from 0 to 1.

points.description:
Regression scatter: the subject first when it has both metrics, then
every peer with both metrics in universe order. Empty without an X
extractor.

regression.description:
Fit of Y on X over the peers that have both, evaluated at the subject:
`fitted_value` is the subject's fitted Y and `residual` its actual less
fitted, in Y units. `None` without an X extractor, without both subject
metrics, or when it cannot be fitted. It can be present on an excluded
dimension.

signal.description:
What this dimension contributes to the composite, positive meaning cheap:
the standardized regression residual, or the z-score without an X
extractor, with the sign set by `direction`. `None` when excluded.

subject_x.description:
Subject's X metric; `None` without an X extractor or when missing or
non-finite.

subject_y.description: Subject's Y metric; `None` when missing or non-finite.

x.description:
X metric extractor; `None` for a dimension scored on its peer
distribution.

z_score.description:
Subject's raw z-score within those peer Y values, before the direction
convention is applied.

d_d48fd91f6cb32ab6859b.description:
Rich/cheap sign convention for a scoring dimension's Y metric.

Determines how a higher-than-peers Y value maps onto the composite
score (positive = cheap). Spread- and yield-like metrics are cheap
when high ([`HigherIsCheap`](Self::HigherIsCheap)); valuation
multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA) are rich when high
([`HigherIsRich`](Self::HigherIsRich)).

The direction is applied consistently to both the regression-residual
path and the univariate z-score path. The default,
`HigherIsCheap`, matches the historical regression-path convention
(positive residual = actual spread above fitted fair spread = cheap).

oneOf.description: Higher Y than peers means the subject is cheap (spread-like metrics).
Higher Y than peers means the subject is rich (multiple-like metrics).
